newsitem.title: USA: New delays in Staples, Office Depot merger.
newsitem.headline: New delays in Staples, Office Depot merger.

text.p: Staples and Office Depot said on Friday the government is allowing the office superstore chains more time for negotiations on a proposed merger, extending a critical deadline from March 5 to March 13.

At the same time, the Federal Trade Commission announced it had cancelled an unusual Saturday session. The merger, which has raised antitrust concerns among regulators, was the subject of that meeting, sources close to the talks said.
Without an agreement to extend the deadline, the commissioners may have voted Saturday to seek a court injunction halting the merger as anticompetitive.
The two office superstore chains said in September they would merge, creating a company with more than 1,117 stores in the United States and annual revenues of more than $10 billion.
But they soon ran into regulatory difficulties as the FTC balked at the idea of creating a superstore superchain.
As a result, the companies have sought one extension after another under provisions of the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act.
The act puts the government under a deadline to decide whether to approve mergers. The time limit generally works in favour of companies, which want mergers approved quickly.
But when a proposed merger runs into trouble it is companies that seek delay, so they may negotiate a restructured deal with the government.
If no agreement can be reached, the government will ultimately go into court to halt the merger as a violation of antitrust laws.
In the past few days, senior FTC staff members and representatives of the companies have engaged in hard-nosed bargaining, say those familiar with the talks.
Analysts speculate the government and the two companies are wrangling over how many stores the two companies would have to divest if they merged.
Staples has 490 office superstores in the United States and Office Depot 527. The only other office superstore chain is OfficeMax.
At issue in the talks has been the definition of the market served by the office superstores.
If office superstores compete primarily with each other, then the government would be reluctant to allow the number of competitors to drop from three to two.
But representatives of Staples and Office Depot argue that they are a small part of a much larger market for office supplies and equipment.
Staples' stock rose 43.75 cents to $21.625 on Nasdaq. Office Depot edged up 37.5 cents to $19 on the New York Stock Exchange.
